8400.full: συν-απ-άγω [in LXX: Exo.14:6 (לָקַח) * ;] to lead away with or together (Ex, l.with). Pass., metaphorically (as συμπεριφέρομαι, see LS, see word), to be carried away with: with dative, Gal.2:13, 2Pe.3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163), Rom.12:16.† (AS)

s: to be counted with others, to be taken into account
8401.full: to reckon in, to take into the account, enumerate , (Isaeus Orator); so in Mid., (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass. to be counted with others, to be taken into account , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

8407.full: συν-αίρω [in LXX: Exo.23:5 (עָזַב) * ;] to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mat.18:23-24; before μετά, C. genitive of person(s), Mat.25:19.† (AS)

8410.full: to bite together , συνδ. τὸ στόμιον of a horse, to take the bit in his teeth , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8417.full: to rear up along with or together , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to grow up with , τινί (Euripides) (ML)

8421.full: Dep.:—; to go or come out with , τινι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to press together, press on all sides
8426.full: συν-θλίβω [in LXX: Ecc.12:6 א A (רָצַץ), Sir.34:14 (31:14), 1Ma.15:14 A * ;] to press together, press on all sides: Mrk.5:24, 31.† (AS)

8429.lxx: in LXX: Zec.8:21 א1 (הָלַךְ), Tob.5:16 א, Wis.6:23 *
8429.full: συν-οδεύω [in LXX: Zec.8:21 א1 (הָלַךְ), Tob.5:16 א, Wis.6:23 * ;] to journey with: with dative of person(s), Act.9:7 (Plut., al.).† (AS)

s: Of various materials, to build up together
8431.full: συν-οίκοδομέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Est.5:68 * ;] __1. to build together or with (with dative of person(s), 1Esdras, l.with). __2. Of various materials, to build up together (Thuc., al.): metaphorically, of Christians, Eph.2:22.† (AS)

s: to meet with, fall in with
8439.full: συν-τυγχάνω [in LXX: 2Ma.8:14 * ;] to meet with, fall in with: with dative of person(s), Luk.8:19.† (AS)

s: to draw out along with, to help to draw out
8442.full: 1. to draw together, to draw up, contract , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to draw out along with, to help to draw out , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8443.full: 1. knowing along with another, conscious , ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are witnesses , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 2. with accusative (with the verbal construction), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά conscious of many evils, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

8444.full: 1. to sing with or together , (Aeschines Orator); ς. ᾠδάν (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. generally, to be in accord with , τινί (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. transitive to celebrate together , τινά (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

8447.full: 1. to draw together, draw up, contract , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to draw together by stitching, sew together , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Mid. to draw along with one , (Plutarch) (ML)

s: ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering
8453.full: 1. likely to make one stumble or trip : metaphorically slippery, perilous, dangerous , Lat. lubricus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; σφαλερόν [ ἐστι], with infinitive, it is dangerous to . ., (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. σφάλλομαι); ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφ. σύμμαχοι (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

8459.full: to bind tight, bind fast , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

8463.g: a piece of measured out land

8464.full: 1. one who lives at ease , (Plutarch) 2. as adjective leisurely, idle , βίος (Plutarch) (ML)

8465.full: 1. properly to let loose : hence to slit, open , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. φλέβα to open a vein, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. to let fall, drop , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to let go , σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let the mind go, given it play , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off the engines, (Plutarch) 4. to check, stop, stay , Lat. inhibere, κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, (Pindar); σχάσον ὄμμα lower thine eyes, (Euripides):—;Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt one's horsemanship, "given up the turf," (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

8466.full: σχῆμα, -τος, τό (ἔχω), [in LXX: Isa.3:17 (פֹּת) * ;] figure, fashion: 1Co.7:31, Php.2:8.† SYN.: see: μορφή (AS)

8467.full: 1. the mastich-tree , Lat. lentiscus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. its fruit , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a squill , = σκίλλα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: to provide with bodily strength, to recruit
8468.full: 1. to make into a body, to consolidate, organise , (Polybius Historicus) 2. to provide with bodily strength, to recruit , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

8469.full: by heaps, in heaps , [variant datesAnthology Palantina from σωρός (ML)

8471.full: σωφρόνως adv., [in LXX: Wis.9:11 * ;] with sound mind, prudently, soberly: Tit.2:12.† (AS)

8474.full: 1. mostly in plural covering: the covering of a shield , (Euripides): a large cloak , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. a pack-saddle , (Strabo Geographus) 3. a pile , ὅπλων (Plutarch) (ML)

8476.full: 1. called together, summoned , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. ς. ἐκκλησία at Athens, an assembly specially summoned by the στρατηγός (opposite to the ordinary meetings, αἱ κυρίαι); Decret. quoted in (Demosthenes Orator):—;generally, σύγκλητος (i.e. ἐκκλησία); a legislative body , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

8478.full: a mixing together, commixture, blending, tempering , (Thucydides), etc. (ML)

s: in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable
in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical
8481.full: 1. commensurate with another thing, (Euripides): exactly fitting , (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷδε τἀνδρὶ ξ. being of like age with , (Sophocles Tragicus); ποίᾳ σύμμετρος τύχ; coincident with what chance? i. e. in the very nick of time, (Sophocles Tragicus); see. infr. III. 2. 2. commensurable , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. in measure with, proportionable, exactly suitable , (Isocrates Orator), etc. 4. absolute in right measure, in due proportion, symmetrical , opposite to ὑπερβάλλων and ἐλλείπων, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 5. generally, fitting, meet, due , (Aeschulus Tragicus);—; σύμμετρος ὡς κλύειν within fit distance for hearing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. adverb -τρως, (Isocrates Orator), etc. 7. in due time , (Euripides) (ML)

8486.full: one who lives in the same tent, a messmate , Lat. contubernalis, (Thucydides) (ML)

8491.full: 1. a band, riband, fillet , especially a head-band , worn in sign of victory, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 2. a strip or tongue of land , (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

8492.full: τακτός, -ή, -όν (τάσσω), [in LXX: Job.12:5 (שַׁאֲנָן) * ;] ordered, fixed, stated: ἡμέρα, Act.12:21,† (AS)

8493.full: 1. one who carves and distributes, a dispenser , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as the dispenser of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers, a controller, director , (Pindar); τ. κώμων master of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός the priest of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. in Prose, a controller of payments, treasurer , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 3. at Rome, the quaestor , (Plutarch) (ML)

8494.full: 1. to stretch, strain, stretch out , (Iliad by Homer); τ. βιόν to string a bow, (Odyssey by Homer); and in Mid., τόξον τανυσσάμενος having strung his bow, (Iliad by Homer):—;of putting the strings to a harp, ἐτάνυσσε χορδήν (Odyssey by Homer); τ. κανόνα to push the weaving-bar tight , i. e. to weave, (Iliad by Homer); ὅπως τανύσηι when he reins in [the horses, 8th/7th c.BC]; ἐπὶ Ἀκράγαντι τανύσσας (i.e. ὀϊστούς) having aimed them, (Pindar):—;Pass., γναθμοὶ τάνυσθεν (for ἐτανύσθησαν) the hollow cheeks filled out , (Odyssey by Homer); to run at full stretch , of horses galloping, (Homer) 2. metaphorically to strain, make more intense , μάχην (Iliad by Homer); ἔριδα πολέμοιο πεῖραρ τάνυσσαν strained the tug of war, (Iliad by Homer) 3. to stretch out, lay along, lay , (Homer); τ. τινὰ ἐν κονίηις, ἐπὶ γαίηι to lay one in the dust, stretch him at his length , (Homer):—;Pass. to lie stretched out , (Homer): to extend , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς (Iliad by Homer):—;also, τρίβος τετάνυστο the path stretched away , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

8497.full: 1. lowness of stature, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of condition, low estate, abasement , (Thucydides) 3. lowness of spirits, dejection , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. in moral sense, baseness, vileness , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

8498.full: ταπεινόφρων, -ον (ταπεινός, φρήν), [in LXX: Pro.29:23 (רוּחַ שָׁפָל)* ;] humble-minded: 1Pe.3:8 (in bad sense, Plut., 2, 336 E, cf. Deiss., LAE, 72.3).† (AS)
